messages.subject: Variables declared in model block not saved?
parts:
Hi folks,

Possibly a quick'un. Is there any reason that variables declared in the model block are not saved? Take this example of a 1D Gaussian Process model

data {
    // nX: num unique X values
    int<lower=1> nX ; 
    // X: unique x values
    vector[nX] X ; 
    // nY: number of observations total
    int<lower=1> nY ;
    // Y: data 
    vector[nY] Y ;
    // XY: *index* of x value per observation in Y 
    int XY[nY] ;
    // fudge: a fudge factor for computation
    real<lower=0> fudge ;
  }
  transformed data {
    // dx: computing the pairwise distances between x values
    matrix[nX,nX] dx ;
    //off-diagonal
    for (i in 1:(nX-1)) {
      for (j in (i+1):nX) {
        dx[i,j] = -( X[i] - X[j] )^2  ;
        dx[j,i] = dx[i,j] ; // lower mirrors upper
      }
    }
    //diagonal
    for (nx in 1:nX){
      dx[nx,nx] = 0 ;
    }
  }
  parameters {
    // noise: sampling noise for replicates
    real<lower=0> noise ;
    // eta_intercept: GP parameter, scale of output (Y)
    real<lower=0> eta ;
    // rho_intercept: GP parameter, x-axis scale of influence between points (wiggliness)
    real<lower=0> rho ;
    // z: dummy variable for quicker multivariate normal computation for GP
    vector[nX] z ;
  }
  model {
    // f: function values
    vector[nX] f ;
    // priors on GP kernel parameters
    eta ~ weibull(2,1) ;
    rho ~ student_t(4,0,1) ;
    // prior on noise
    noise ~ weibull(2,1) ;
    z ~ normal(0,1) ;
    {
      // L: cholesky decomposition
      matrix[nX,nX] L ;
      // covMat: covariance matrix
      matrix[nX,nX] covMat ;
      //  covMat off-diagonal
      for (i in 1:(nX-1)) {
        for (j in (i+1):nX) {
          covMat[i,j] = eta * exp(dx[i,j]*rho) ;
          covMat[j,i] = covMat[i,j] ; // lower mirrors upper
        }
      }
      // covMat diagonal: adding jitter to avoid computation issues ??
      for (nx in 1:nX){
        covMat[nx,nx] = eta + fudge ; 
      }  
      L = cholesky_decompose(covMat) ;
      // assert sampling of f as zero-centered GP
      f = L * z ;
    }
    // assert sampling of each replicate of Y as GP plus noise
    Y ~ normal(f[XY],noise) ;
  }

This runs fine, but the variable "f" isn't in the rstan::stanfit object. I know the variables declared in the local block within the model block (ex. L & covMat) won't be saved for access in the stanfit object, but I would have thought "f" would be. I know the solution is to declare f in the transformed parameters block, and cut-and-paste the entire local block currently (in the above code) in the model block to the transformed parameters block, yielding:

  data {
    // nX: num unique X values
    int<lower=1> nX ; 
    // X: unique x values
    vector[nX] X ; 
    // nY: number of observations total
    int<lower=1> nY ;
    // Y: data 
    vector[nY] Y ;
    // XY: *index* of x value per observation in Y 
    int XY[nY] ;
    // fudge: a fudge factor for computation
    real<lower=0> fudge ;
  }
  transformed data {
    // dx: computing the pairwise distances between x values
    matrix[nX,nX] dx ;
    //off-diagonal
    for (i in 1:(nX-1)) {
      for (j in (i+1):nX) {
        dx[i,j] = -( X[i] - X[j] )^2  ;
        dx[j,i] = dx[i,j] ; // lower mirrors upper
      }
    }
    //diagonal
    for (nx in 1:nX){
      dx[nx,nx] = 0 ;
    }
  }
  parameters {
    // noise: sampling noise for replicates
    real<lower=0> noise ;
    // eta_intercept: GP parameter, scale of output (Y)
    real<lower=0> eta ;
    // rho_intercept: GP parameter, x-axis scale of influence between points (wiggliness)
    real<lower=0> rho ;
    // z: dummy variable for quicker multivariate normal computation for GP
    vector[nX] z ;
  }
  transformed parameters{
    // f: function values
    vector[nX] f ;
    {
      // L: cholesky decomposition
      matrix[nX,nX] L ;
      // covMat: covariance matrix
      matrix[nX,nX] covMat ;
      //  covMat off-diagonal
      for (i in 1:(nX-1)) {
        for (j in (i+1):nX) {
          covMat[i,j] = eta * exp(dx[i,j]*rho) ;
          covMat[j,i] = covMat[i,j] ; // lower mirrors upper
        }
      }
      // covMat diagonal: adding jitter to avoid computation issues ??
      for (nx in 1:nX){
        covMat[nx,nx] = eta + fudge ; 
      }  
      L = cholesky_decompose(covMat) ;
      // assert sampling of f as zero-centered GP
      f = L * z ;
    }
  }
  model {
    // priors on GP kernel parameters
    eta ~ weibull(2,1) ;
    rho ~ student_t(4,0,1) ;
    // prior on noise
    noise ~ weibull(2,1) ;
    z ~ normal(0,1) ;
    // assert sampling of each replicate of Y as GP plus noise
    Y ~ normal(f[XY],noise) ;
  }

But for teaching purposes I thought it might be more straightforward to omit the transformed parameters block altogether. That said, I just noticed that the version using the transformed parameters block actually computes with better ESS/time; any idea why that might be?

Thanks!

Mike

I set it up that way originally because it seemed natural
to put any transforms together in one block and save the
transformed parameters, then put all the density statements
in the model block. Just seemed like the natural organization
for programming a model.

We have toyed with two competing ideas:

1. eliminating transformed parameters and saving variables
at top of model block, and

2. adding jacobian += statements to the transformed parameters
block that would add to the Jacobian for the transformed (it
is controlled by the algorithms---the Jacobian is turned off
for optimization)

- Bob

Ok, I've tested this on a PC running linux and a Mac, in addition to the Linux VM running on Google's compute engine. All have lots of RAM (min 16GB) and fast CPUs, and all are running Stan v2.11 via RStan. For a given machine, I computed all models while the machine was doing relatively little else, using single chain single core sampling (i.e. no parallel chains), and interleaving multiple sampling runs of the models.

The results are weird.

Here's a gist of the code for my experimentation:
https://gist.github.com/mike-lawrence/96d14bac6264b5f4eff4f3d7001acec9

The R file is what generates data and samples the models (using the same seed when comparing the different models).

"tp0.stan" is a version that uses transformed parameters, "tp1.stan" is a version that uses a local block at the very top of the model block, and "tp2.stan" is what I use to look at the consequence of putting the local block in the model block at different places. Why would I put it at different places? Because I discovered that, regardless of machine, when the local block is at the top of the model block, as in tp1 I get identical performance & samples as I get with tp0". However, if I move the location of that local block around within the model block, I get different timing and samples from tp0. As a summary:

Machine: Linux VM on Google
- tp2 local block @ beginning: same samples and timing as tp0
- tp2 local block @ end: initialization errors, model can't sample
- tp2 local block anywhere in middle: different samples from tp0, slower by 30% *if* placed right before the last line (this happened to be the position that I used earlier, hence my report of the 30% timing difference), else same timing as tp0

Machine: Linux PC & Mac OS X (same story on both)
- tp2 local block @ beginning: same samples and timing as tp0
- tp2 local block @ end: initialization errors, model can't sample
- tp2 local block anywhere in middle: different samples from tp0, same timing as tp0

So, the previously reported timing difference only occurs with the Linux VM on Google compute engine, and only when the local block is placed at a very specific location in the model block. Leaving that mystery as probably too hardware involved to bother with, a remaining mystery is that, for all platforms, placement of the local block at anywhere but the beginning of the model block yields different samples from the version that uses the transformed parameters section, and placement of the local block at the end of the model block yields initialization errors that prevent sampling. Presumably this is not expected behaviour? 

Other weirdness: despite setting the random seed both in R when generating fake data and in the calls to rstan::sampling(), I seem to be getting different samples from machine to machine. Is my expectation that I should be getting the same samples naive?

Mike

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variables declared in model block not saved?
parts:
Remember that everything in the transformed parameters block is computed one extra time per sample vs. quantities that are put in the model block. When the transformations are computationally expensive, like building a covariance matrix and doing a cholesky decomposition on that matrix, you'll notice that a model that uses a transformed parameters block will be a bit slower than a model that puts the computation in the model block.

Rob

parts:
No, I'm talking about the call to write_array that reruns the transformed parameters block with doubles once per iteration. I only figured this out because I wanted to make sure my rev specialization of cov_exp_quad was getting called during sampling so I put cout calls in both rev and prim versions and found that the prim version got called once per post-warmup sample (I assume because I hadn't elected to save warmup samples).

Rob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variables declared in model block not saved?
parts:
I meant it has to run the generated quantities block, not the
model block---we shouldn't need the Jacobian for the parameter
constraints or the model block. If that's not how it's set up,
it could be. The step that produces the final parameters
will have already evaluated the density, so we only need to compute
the generated quantities in write_array and we can do it without
derivatives with double values. This is why I think of it as
the generated quantities generator.

- Bob
